'''Shaun Edward Alexander''' (born August 30, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] and [[Washington Redskins]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 1999. He was selected by the Seahawks 19th overall in the [[2000 NFL draft]]. In 2011, he was inducted into the [[Alabama Sports Hall of Fame]].

Alexander set numerous NFL and Seahawks' franchise records and was named the [[National Football League Most Valuable Player Award|NFL MVP]] in 2005.  He was also named to the NFL's 2000 All-Decade team,<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 31, 2010 |title=League announces 2000s NFL All-Decade Team |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/league-announces-2000s-nfl-all-decade-team-09000d5d8161b0e9 |access-date=August 14, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> and is tied in ranking ninth all time in NFL history for rushing touchdowns (100). Alexander was the first athlete featured on the cover of both the ''[[NCAA Football (video game series)#NCAA Football 2001|NCAA Football]]'' and ''[[Madden NFL 07|Madden NFL]]'' series of video games.
